extraction_method: HYBRID. (1) The set of 20 app.include_router() mount points is HAND-ENUMERATED from platform/python-sidecar/main.py — verified exhaustive via `grep -rn include_router` across the whole python-sidecar tree (zero other call sites exist). (2) The per-router endpoint list (path + method) is MECHANICALLY cross-checked two ways: (a) each router file's own @router.get/@router.post decorators were grepped directly, and (b) a live GET /openapi.json snapshot was fetched from the deployed amjis-sidecar Cloud Run service on 2026-07-20 (see openapi_snapshot.json in this directory) and diffed against (a) — the two agree exactly, zero missing / zero extra paths (see validation block below). (3) health_probe, concurrency_cap, and cost_class fields are HAND-AUTHORED v1 judgments — no per-router health-check or concurrency metadata exists anywhere in this codebase to extract mechanically; these are conservative defaults, not measurements.

deploy_flags_as_of_snapshot.concurrency_effective: Cloud Run platform default (80 concurrent requests per container instance) — deploy.yml does not pass --concurrency, verified by reading the `flags:` block of the deploy-sidecar job

sidecar_service.auth: x-api-key header (PYTHON_SIDECAR_API_KEY secret via Secret Manager), enforced per-router via FastAPI `Depends(verify_api_key)` passed to each app.include_router() call. NOT applied to /health, /docs, /openapi.json — those are unauthenticated by construction (confirmed: openapi_snapshot.json in this directory was fetched with no API key).

health_probe.existing_ts_side_probe: platform/src/app/api/sidecar/health/route.ts — server-side proxy for this endpoint (auth-gated to logged-in users; adds a 5s AbortSignal.timeout)

sidecar_service.process_model: SINGLE FastAPI process. All 20 routers below (49 endpoints) plus /health run in the same Cloud Run service/container — there is NO per-router process or concurrency isolation today. A concurrency problem in one router (e.g. an expensive PyJHora compute) can starve every other router sharing the same instance.
sidecar_service.concurrency_note: No per-router concurrency caps exist in the running system — this is the honest v1 finding, not a gap in this manifest. The only real ceiling is Cloud Run's shared per-instance concurrency (80, platform default, NOT overridden in deploy.yml) applied across ALL 50 endpoints in this one process, with min-instances=0 (cold starts possible) and cpu=2 (so CPU-bound compute routers — ephemeris, pyhora, panchang, phala muhurta/holistic_bundle — will bottleneck on CPU well before hitting the 80-request ceiling). The per-router `cost_class` field below (cheap / medium / expensive) is a hand-authored QUALITATIVE judgment of compute weight per request, read from each handler's own code (DB-only read = cheap; ephemeris/dasha/panchang derivation = medium; full natal/electional/holistic-bundle multi-technique compute = expensive) — it is NOT a measured number and NOT independently enforced (no semaphore, no queue, no per-route rate limit exists anywhere in main.py or the router files). Actually adding per-route concurrency isolation (e.g. a semaphore per cost_class) is W2 scope if the native wants it, not landed here.

Not referenced anywhere in .github/workflows/deploy.yml (grep-verified). The live PyHora integration path is routers/pyhora.py, mounted IN-PROCESS inside the single amjis-sidecar service at /api/pyhora (see routers entry above) — it imports pyjhora_adapter's submodules directly rather than calling a second HTTP service. Conclusion: pyhora.Dockerfile is dead/orphaned build infra, not a second deployed service. This means the real router count is the 20 enumerated above (single service), not 20+a-second-pyhora-service as a naive Dockerfile inventory might suggest. Flagged for the native; not deleted or fixed here (out of L1c scope — this lane documents, W2+ or a hygiene pass can clean it up).
